title: ROUTR
oneLiner: Small router skills that send an AI coding agent to the right workflow before it reads anything.
shortSummary: Open-source routing layer for AI coding agents. Each router matches a situation from its description alone and tells the agent which skills to read, in what order, and what to skip.
longSummary: An agent with dozens of installed skills tends to pick the wrong one and read whole files to find out, burning its context window. ROUTR puts a thin layer in front: 28 routr-* router skills with explicit “use when / not for” descriptions, so routing is decided from the slash-menu text and only the one full playbook needed gets loaded. Requests that span several workflows get a route plan of at most three steps, with one router active at a time.
responsibilities: Designed the router format: a tight “Use when / Not for” description, an exit condition and a handoff
Wrote the 28 router skills and the routes.json file that defines handoffs, companions and chains
Built the skill validator that runs in CI on every change
Wrote the 153-prompt single-router eval set plus multi-route and held-out chain prompts, and ran the blind evaluations
constraints: Routing has to work from short descriptions alone — the agent should not load a playbook to decide whether it needs it
Real requests span several workflows, but two routers active at once would contradict each other
Child skills may not be installed, so every router needs a fallback
outcomes: MIT-licensed and installable with one command

Blind runs with a model that saw only the prompt file and menu reached 99.3% and 97.4% router accuracy on the 153-prompt set, as reported in the README; the method is published so the numbers can be reproduced
Route plans capped at three steps, with one active router and at most one companion checklist per step
Missing child skills fall back to built-in routr-depth-* skills instead of failing
learnings: Description text is the routing interface — the “not for” boundaries matter as much as the “use when” ones
Chain prompts written before the composition rules, and never used for tuning, give a more honest measure than a tuned set
seoDescription: ROUTR: open-source router skills that match an AI coding agent’s request to the right workflow, with a CI validator and a published routing eval. Built by Mohamed Aslam.
